title: Canonical cotangent comparison for squares with zero relative complexes
statement:
Let $A\to B$, $A'\to B'$, $a:A\to A'$ and $b:B\to B'$ be a commutative square of homomorphisms of commutative rings. Use the standard cotangent complexes and their standard square maps [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence], in the derived categories of ordinary modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume $L_{A'/A}=0$ in $D(A')$ and $L_{B'/B}=0$ in $D(B')$. Then the canonical morphism
$$\beta_{a,b}:L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B'\longrightarrow L_{B'/A'}$$
is an isomorphism in $D(B')$. Here $\beta_{a,b}$ is the composite of the first functoriality arrow for the triple $A\to B\to B'$ and the second functoriality arrow for $A\to A'\to B'$; equivalently it is the derived scalar-extension adjoint of the standard square map. This specifies the morphism, not just the existence of an isomorphism. For two successive squares satisfying these vanishing hypotheses, the composite of their comparison morphisms, after derived extension of scalars and the derived tensor associator, equals the comparison for the composite square. Identity squares give identity comparisons.
If in addition $B'$ is flat over $B$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], then $B'[0]$ is K-flat [def-pc-module-kflat-complex], and for every complex $K$ of $B$-modules the derived-to-ordinary tensor comparison identifies $K\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B'$ with the termwise complex $K\otimes_B B'$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Under this identification, $\beta_{a,b}$ is represented by the canonical chain map $L^{\mathrm{std}}_{B/A}\otimes_B B'\to L^{\mathrm{std}}_{B'/A'}$ and that map is a quasi-isomorphism. For successive squares with flat maps on the upper rings, their ordinary chain comparisons compose under $(x\otimes c)\otimes d\mapsto x\otimes b'(c)d$, where $b':B'\to B''$ is the second upper-ring map; this is the same equality as for their derived comparisons. No tensor-pushout hypothesis on the square is assumed.

proof.text: Write $C=L^{\mathrm{std}}_{B/A}$ and $C'=L^{\mathrm{std}}_{B'/A'}$. Their standard square map is a $B$-linear chain map $\gamma:C\to\operatorname{Res}_b C'$ by [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. Each term of $C$ is free over $B$: apply [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables] to the polynomial term of the standard resolution, then tensor its differential basis with $B$. Such a free module is flat directly, since tensoring with it is a direct sum of copies of the original map, and direct sums preserve exactness componentwise. Since $C^i=0$ for $i>0$, [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] makes $C$ K-flat. The same holds for the standard complexes of every ring map used below. Transport [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] through [lem-trf-one-point-derived-ring-identification]. If $c_C:L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B'\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(C\otimes_B B')$ is its canonical computation isomorphism, the adjunct of $Q\gamma$ is $Q(m)c_C$, where $m(x\otimes c)=c\gamma(x)$. This defines $\beta_{a,b}$ with the required normalization, for arbitrary ring squares.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-cotangent-transitivity-triangle] to $A\to B\to B'$. It gives the distinguished triangle $L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B'\xrightarrow{f}L_{B'/A}\to L_{B'/B}\to(L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B')[1]$. Its third object is zero by hypothesis, so [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero] makes $f$ invertible. The cited triangle specifies $f$ as the first standard functoriality arrow, rather than an arbitrarily chosen isomorphism.

Apply [lem-trf-cotangent-transitivity-triangle] to $A\to A'\to B'$. The first term $L_{A'/A}\otimes_{A'}^{\mathbf L}B'$ is zero: derived change of rings is an exact additive functor by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], specialized to modules by [lem-trf-one-point-derived-ring-identification], and therefore preserves zero objects. Rotate this triangle to put its second arrow $g:L_{B'/A}\to L_{B'/A'}$ first; its third term is the shift of a zero object. Rotation and shift are those of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero] makes $g$ invertible. The original square is the composite of the squares $(A\to B)\to(A\to B')$ and $(A\to B')\to(A'\to B')$. Standard square maps compose by [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. Naturality of the adjunction in [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] says that postcomposing the adjunct $f$ with $g$ is the adjunct of their composite square map. Thus $\beta_{a,b}=gf$, which is invertible. Neither triangle required a tensor pushout.

proof.text: For successive squares write $F_b=-\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B'$, $R_b=\operatorname{Res}_b$, and similarly for $b':B'\to B''$, with units $\eta_b$. Let their standard square maps in derived categories be $\gamma,\gamma'$. By [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], $R_b(\beta)\eta_b=\gamma$ and $R_{b'}(\beta')\eta_{b'}=\gamma'$, using the one-point identification [lem-trf-one-point-derived-ring-identification]. The associator $F_{b'}F_b\cong F_{b'b}$ identifies its unit with the composite units by [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization]. Writing $C=L_{B/A}$ and $C'=L_{B'/A'}$, naturality gives $R_{b'}F_{b'}(\beta)\eta_{b',F_bC}=\eta_{b',C'}\beta$. Together with the composite-unit formula, this makes the adjunct of $\beta'F_{b'}(\beta)$ equal to $R_b(\gamma')\gamma$. By [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] this is the square map for the composite. Bijectivity of adjunction proves the asserted equality of comparisons. For the identity square the square map is the identity; its adjunct is the scalar-unit identification, hence the identity after $F_{1_B}\cong\mathrm{id}$. Also the composite squares satisfy the vanishing hypotheses: apply [lem-trf-cotangent-transitivity-triangle] to $A\to A'\to A''$ and $B\to B'\to B''$; their outer terms are zero by the assumed vanishings and preservation of zero by derived change of rings, so their middle terms vanish by [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero].

proof.text: Now suppose $B'$ is flat over $B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], tensor with $B'$ preserves short exact sequences. For an acyclic $F$, tensor the sequences $0\to Z^iF\to F^i\to Z^{i+1}F\to0$: the images and kernels of the tensored differentials agree. Thus $F\otimes_B B'$ is acyclic, which says exactly that $B'[0]$ is K-flat by [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. More generally, put $D^iK=\operatorname{im}d^{i-1}$. Tensor the exact sequences $0\to Z^iK\to K^i\to D^{i+1}K\to0$ and $0\to D^iK\to Z^iK\to H^iK\to0$. Their kernels and quotients give $H^i(K\otimes_B B')=H^i(K)\otimes_B B'$, naturally in chain maps, so tensor preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $q:P\to K$ by [lem-pc-source-module-kflat-resolution]. Use the derived-change-of-rings pair and natural derived-to-ordinary counit $\varepsilon$ of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, lem-trf-one-point-derived-ring-identification]. Its computation map $c_P=\varepsilon_P$ is invertible. Naturality gives $\varepsilon_K=Q(q\otimes1)c_P(F_b(Qq))^{-1}$. Each factor is invertible, including $Q(q\otimes1)$ by the preceding exactness calculation. This is precisely the canonical identification $F_b(QK)\cong Q(K\otimes_B B')$, for every unbounded $K$.

source.place: Tags 06XZ (definition-K-flat), 06Y4 (lemma-K-flat-resolution), and 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change), together with algebra.tex Tag 00HD (lemma-flat); explicit natural-counit calculation for a flat coefficient module.

proof.text: For $K=C$, the counit $\varepsilon_C$ of Step 5 is the same canonical computation map $c_C$ used in Step 1: [lem-trf-one-point-derived-ring-identification] transports the derived pair and its counit, and [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] uses that computation map on flat-term K-flat representatives. Its normalized adjunct formula therefore gives $\beta_{a,b}=Q(m)\varepsilon_C$ for the canonical chain map $m:C\otimes_B B'\to C'$, $x\otimes c\mapsto c\gamma(x)$. Since $\beta$ and $\varepsilon_C$ are invertible, $Q(m)$ is invertible. Each cohomology functor factors through $Q$ by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; hence $H^i(m)$ is invertible for every $i$, so $m$ is a quasi-isomorphism. This proves the claim for the specified map, not merely for an isomorphic pair of objects.

proof.text: For two successive flat upper-ring maps, let $m,m'$ be these chain comparisons, and $\gamma,\gamma'$ the standard semilinear maps. On a pure tensor $((x\otimes c)\otimes d)$ their composite is $d\,\gamma'(c\gamma(x))=b'(c)d\,(\gamma'\gamma)(x)$. By [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence], $\gamma'\gamma$ is exactly the composite-square map. This is the value of its chain comparison on $x\otimes b'(c)d$, so the chain maps agree under the stated associator, since pure tensors generate. The associator represents the derived associator by [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization], and its units and the normalized adjuncts agree with those of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Consequently the chain equality localizes to exactly the equality in Step 4.
